discovery: Experimental demonstration of fractional charge and anyonic exchange statistics of quasiparticles in the fractional quantum Hall effect

nominees.name: Gwendal Fève
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'École Normale Supérieure, Paris, France

subfield: Condensed matter physics (experimental quantum Hall physics, anyons)
motivation: Anyons, particles that are neither bosons nor fermions, were predicted to exist as quasiparticles of fractional quantum Hall states, carrying fractions of the electron charge and acquiring nontrivial phases when exchanged. For decades this remained theory. Heiblum pioneered shot-noise measurements that directly revealed fractional charges e/3 and later e/4, establishing quantum transport as a probe of emergent quasiparticles. In 2020 two complementary experiments finally exposed anyonic statistics: Fève and collaborators built an anyon collider whose cross-correlations revealed the braiding phase, and Manfra's group, using exceptionally clean heterostructures he engineered, observed discrete phase slips in a Fabry-Pérot interferometer matching the predicted exchange phase. Together these works turned anyons from mathematical objects into measured physical entities, opening the experimental path toward non-Abelian anyons and topologically protected quantum information.
